explanations.answer: He gives it to some of the tribes as an inheritance
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. The text says Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites struck the kings down and "…given their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh." Three groups, and all three got a share. I'd love to say I handed out cookies that fairly, but I always ate the broken ones first (Joshua 12:6).

explanations.answer: He holds it for himself as Israel's leader
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Joshua 12:6 says Moses and the Israelites struck the kings down and the land was given "…as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh." The text calls Moses "…the servant of the LORD…" and says nothing about him keeping any of it. The land goes to those three groups. Nobody's holding the whole batch for himself here.

explanations.answer: He sets it aside until the war is over
explanations.explanation: Good guess, because waiting is a real thing. But this passage doesn't say the land sat on a shelf. It says Moses and the Israelites struck the kings down and "…given their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 12:6). Handed over, done, no cooling rack needed.

Joshua it is, baker! Verse 7 says, "…these are the kings of the land that Joshua and the Israelites conquered beyond the Jordan to the west…" Moses handled the east, and Joshua took the west. Two leaders, two sides of the river, and one very long list.

Caleb is a fine name, but the text doesn't give him this job. Joshua 12:7 says, "…these are the kings of the land that Joshua and the Israelites conquered beyond the Jordan to the west…" The leader named there is Joshua. Don't feel bad, friend, I once mixed up my own mustache with a whisk.

Aaron's a big name in the Bible, so I see why he came to mind. But in this passage the west side belongs to someone else: "…the kings of the land that Joshua and the Israelites conquered…" (Joshua 12:7). Joshua is the one named as leading the Israelites there. Aaron isn't in this roll call at all.

Close, friend, but not quite. Joshua and the Israelites did conquer those kings, and that part is true. But the text says Joshua gave the land as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, "according to the allotments to the tribes of Israel…" (Joshua 12:7). So he won it and handed it out. It doesn't say he kept it under his own rule.

False is right, baker! The text says Joshua gave the land to the tribes as an inheritance, "according to the allotments to the tribes of Israel…" (Joshua 12:7). He won it, then handed it out. That's a leader who finishes a batch and shares the whole box.
